material_definitions: The electrical properties and the crystal structure were investigated for the ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The conductivity enhanced by the Li20 addition with LiHf2 (PO4) 3 system and by the increase of x for Li1+xMxHf2-x (PO4) 3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu or Y) systems.
The P21/n monoclinic phase transformed to NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase at above 1173 K.
The activation energy for bulk component was 0.42 eV for the NASICON-type structure.
The material system investigated is LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O where y ranges from 0 to 0.4.
Li2O acts as a flux, helping to obtain high density pellets and decrease the porosity.
Sintering at or above 1293 K induces a phase transition from the monoclinic (P21/n) phase to the high-conductivity NASICON-type rhombohedral (R3c) phase.
The maximum conductivity was achieved for samples sintered around 1298 K.
The electrical properties were studied for ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The materials are solid solutions of $Li_{1+x}M_xHf_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$ (M=Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y) sintered above 1293 K to achieve maximum conductivity and a NASICON-type structure.
The high density pellets were generally obtained by increasing x, except for M=Cr.
The conductivity enhancement is attributed to high densification and the decrease in the activation energy at the grain boundary.
The specific sample $Li_{1.2}Fe_{0.2}Hf_{1.8}(PO_4)_3$ corresponds to x=0.2 in the $M=Fe$ system and showed maximum conductivity.
